correctness.rationale: The cut complex is rebuilt from the definition: 32 disconnected triples give face vector (8,28,56,64,32), and exact rational boundary ranks (7,21,35,28) give reduced homology only in degrees 3 and 4 with dimensions 1 and 4. The full 48-element automorphism group is obtained by an 8-by-6 lower-and-upper count. An explicit cycle-cocycle pair detects the H_3 scalar for every automorphism, and exact signed fixed-simplex Lefschetz traces determine H_4. All 48 values satisfy the claimed orientation and body-diagonal character formulas. Character equality over Q determines the semisimple representations.

value.rationale: The cube is a canonical highly symmetric graph, and the defining cut-complex literature explicitly treats symmetry actions on rational homology as mathematically significant. This result identifies those actions in a previously nonequivariant mixed-dimensional example: the one-dimensional class transforms by geometric orientation, while the four-dimensional group is a natural parity twist of the four body diagonals. That is structural information not recoverable from Betti numbers or the known wedge type and provides a compact benchmark for equivariant cut-complex phenomena beyond the source's treated families.
